title: Oaths, Shrines, and the Mughal Bid to Split the Panth

blocks.text: The Mughals now try persuasion rather than direct slaughter, swearing kasam kurân bahu bâr uthâvhi so Sikh leaders will trust that protected movement and worship can resume under official guarantees.

They promise access to sacred places such as nankâng au raurdi jai and offer to let congregations assemble wherever relics or gur-thaurs remain, summarized here through melâlâvhu b¢shkai jahin jahin hui gur thaur.

That offer is not innocent: by courting figures like binôd singh au kahan singh and by saying singhan kô bahu paisç dçhin, the state tries to buy division inside the Khalsa rather than defeat it honestly.
